scan-first S3-FIFO: scan_pids pages in own FIFO drained first (GET-hit pages get CLOCK 2nd chance, floor 256 pages); GET pages via S3-FIFO small(10%)/main CLOCK freq<=3/ghost; scan-thread accesses don't raise freq
structural 1/3: scan-first CLOCK. scan_pids folios -> scan FIFO drained first; others in CLOCK main list; 1-byte state in flat ARRAY (no hash maps on hot path); scan folio hit by GET promoted to main
scan-first S3-FIFO (retry after compile fix: renamed need_more/ctx clashes). scan_pids pages in own FIFO drained first, floor 256 pages; GET pages S3-FIFO small 10%/main CLOCK/ghost
structural 1/3 (retry): scan-first CLOCK; state ARRAY index = hash(i_ino, index) since verifier forbids pointer shifts

structural 1/3 scan-offload: ONLY scan_pids-inserted folios on our FIFO list (exact count via small hash), evict oldest scan folios first keeping 256-page reserve; otherwise propose nothing so kernel default LRU handles GET pages. Tests whether kernel falls back for unproposed victims; no folio_accessed hook (zero hot-path cost)
ablation of c5210e3c: drop scan-first list; scan-thread pages enter S3-FIFO small like others, scan accesses still ignored for freq. Tests whether scan-first eviction is what loses to noop
structural 2/3: scan-first freq-CLOCK: main list uses 2-bit freq counter (hit +1 cap 3, hand -1 & requeue, evict at 0), up to 4 hand passes; scan FIFO still drained first. Prev plain CLOCK = 625
calibration: noop (kernel default reclaim) on my host pc257 - true bar + default probe profile; all scan-first attempts so far (488-581) are below stated 630-650

scan-offload 2/3 (ablation of ee0fb848): SCAN_RESERVE 256->2048 pages. Hypothesis: ee0fb848 refaults jumped to 18.4k (vs 11.1k get_scan) because a tiny reserve evicts scan readahead before the scan consumes it. Reflection on ee0fb848: 620 ops/s ~= other scan-first attempts (625); get_scan had FEWER refaults but lower tput, so per-op cost/IO pattern not just refaults matters. NOTE: noop.c as shipped fails to link (S_ISDIR, see d02fff5d) so no host has a true noop number yet

structural 3/3: freq-CLOCK + scan readahead protection: scan-list folios not yet read by scan thread (F_USED) get one requeue before eviction; targets 17k refaults from evicting unconsumed readahead. Prev 641.7

structural 1/3 freq-history: scan-first FIFO (256 reserve) + S3-FIFO-style small/main for GET folios, but frequency is a persistent per-(inode,offset) count in an LRU hash 8x cache, lazily halved every 2^14 GET accesses (TinyLFU-flavour). Admit to main if history>=2; small->main if >=2; main passes evict freq<2,<4,<8,any. Scan-thread accesses don't count.

structural 1/3 history-CLOCK: single CLOCK list, credits<=3; per-page GET freq in LRU hash keyed (inode,index), 4x cgroup pages, outlives eviction, halved every 2^15 GET accesses; refault gets credits=min(count-1,3) even if scan re-read it; scan inserts/accesses add no freq

freq-CLOCK (378d80f2) + ghost LRU_HASH(32k, key ino+index) of evicted main-list folios; ghost-hit refault admitted at freq 2 instead of 0. Scan-list evictions not ghosted. Readahead-protection (8a3c64d0, 630) reverted.

structural 2/3 freq-history (parent bceb7742=602.55): scan list now evicts only folios the scan thread already READ (consumed flag set in folio_accessed for scan pid), no fixed reserve; unread readahead kept up to 2048 pages. Hypothesis: 256-page reserve throws away scan readahead before use -> wasted IOs on an IOPS-limited device (rios ~11K for every policy).

scan-offload structural 3/3 (new sub-idea: readahead-junk filter). Reverted reserve to 256 (2048 gave 602 w/ unchanged refaults 18.7k -> reserve/readahead-loss hypothesis FALSIFIED). New: non-scan folios enter a probation FIFO; on first access they are list_del'd and handed to kernel LRU; eviction = scan FIFO, then never-accessed probation folios (GET readahead pages), else nothing (kernel). Hypothesis: GET-miss readahead pulls pages nobody reads; evicting them first frees cache for hot GET pages
calibration: exact seed noop.c (kernel default reclaim, no struct_ops attach) on pc318, to give my 581/608/591 attempts a same-host baseline (team has no successful noop yet)

ablation of 378d80f2: pure freq-CLOCK, scan-thread folios go into main list like GET folios (no scan-first list). Tests whether scan-first helps; nemo's s3fifo ablation suggested it hurts (scan start keys Zipfian -> ranges re-scanned)

structural 3/3 freq-history: ablate scan-first list (parent 3e1b84bb=604.9). Scan-thread folios enter the S3-FIFO small queue like GET folios; scan reads still don't bump the persistent freq history. Tests nemo's 998b7146 finding (+4.6% from dropping scan-first) inside the freq-history design.

REVIEW/replication: davy-jones 378d80f2 (scan-first freq-CLOCK, team top 641.66 on pc258) resubmitted UNCHANGED (one comment line added) on my host pc252. My scan-offload lane (ee0fb848/b03fc887/572e5ce9 = 620/602/611, refaults stuck 17.8-18.7k) closed after 3 evals: kernel-managed GETs plateau ~610 here. Question: is freq-CLOCK's +3% real cross-host or best-of-N noise? Also: rios ~285/s in EVERY run => disk IOPS-saturated; throughput ~= IOPS x ops-per-IO

S3-FIFO (998b7146, 608) + LevelDB table-tail protection: last 8 pages of each file (index/filter/footer) promoted small->main and skipped by main CLOCK passes 0-2. Tests if table-cache reopen re-reads are a big miss source. pc318 noop=615.7

freq-history + junk-first (parent e4db7979=612.6, no scan-first list): before normal small-queue S3-FIFO eviction, a pass evicts GET-inserted folios never accessed since insertion (readahead neighbours of random GET misses); scan-inserted folios exempt. Hypothesis: IOPS-capped device (rios ~11K constant) + ~4 pages/IO readahead -> small FIFO is mostly junk; evicting it first lengthens probation for real one-hit pages.

calibration: exact seed noop.c on MY host pc252 (+1 comment line). Same-host baseline for my 620/602/611 scan-offload and 591 replication of 378d80f2 (davy's 641 on pc258 did NOT reproduce here: -8%, so cross-host gaps >> 1-2% noise). Pattern on pc252: fewer refaults => LOWER tput (get_scan 11.1k->500, freq-CLOCK 16.1k->591, offload 18k->611); nemo's noop has most refaults (20.4k) at 615.7. rios ~11.5k constant in every run

378d80f2 + probation FIFO: non-scan folios enter new_list (F_NEW), move to main at freq 1 on first non-scan access; eviction order scan FIFO -> new FIFO (floor 64) -> main freq-CLOCK. Targets never-used GET readahead occupying main for a full CLOCK cycle

calibration: exact seed noop.c (from 55919a84) on MY host pc252. CORRECTION: my previous eval 76?/'calibration: exact seed noop' was mislabeled - a failed checkout meant it actually re-ran davy's freq-CLOCK 378d80f2 => 2nd same-host replication = 597.5 (1st 590.9): same-host noise ~1%, while 641 on pc258 is +8% host effect. This is the TRUE noop for pc252, to compare against scan-offload 620/602/611

junk-first 2/3 (parent 14bafa84=630.8): also run the never-accessed-since-insert eviction pass over the main list (ghost/history-admitted readahead neighbours) before frequency-threshold passes. Doubles as a replication check of the junk-first gain (+3.0% vs 612.6).

instrumentation rider on f3a2e20c (S3-FIFO + tail protect, policy unchanged): BPF u64 counters (added scan/get/ghost/tail, accessed scan/get, evicted/evicted_scan/evicted_hit, evict calls/req/got/ns) dumped by loader at exit as JSON to ./policy_metrics.json, ./policy_metrics, /tmp + stdout - probing the policy_counters probe format

REPLICATION of 14bafa84 (630.8; junk-first small pass only), code identical except a comment. Eval fba686fd (+main-list junk pass) gave 619.3 - need to know whether 630.8 was noise before building further.

DIAGNOSTIC: attached no-op. struct_ops attached, all hooks empty, evict_folios proposes 0 victims (kernel fallback does everything). KEY CONTEXT: seed noop (never attaches) = 640.96 on pc252, beating EVERY struct_ops policy I ran here (scan-offload 602-620, davy freq-CLOCK 591/597, get_scan 500). If this scores ~620, merely attaching cache_ext costs ~3% and all policies start in a hole; if ~640, our eviction decisions are what hurt
372e2b1f + 3-bit freq counter (cap 7, was 3), up to 8 hand passes: stronger LFU memory for Zipfian GET pages under LevelDB's block cache. Prev 648.9

FINDING + test. attached no-op 2d090442 = 641.42 ~= seed noop 640.96 on pc252 => attaching cache_ext costs NOTHING; the 3-8% losses come from our eviction choices. ee0fb848 differed from 2d090442 ONLY by scan-first FIFO eviction and lost ~21 (620). Hypothesis: scan pages are NOT junk (YCSB-style scans likely start at Zipfian keys => scans re-cover hot ranges; GETs hit hot keys inside scanned pages), so scan-first eviction hurts. This eval = 572e5ce9 minus scan-first: scan folios unmanaged; only never-accessed GET-readahead folios evicted first, else kernel. >641 => junk filter is a lever; ~641 => kernel near-optimal here

junk-first 3/3, O(1) version (parent 14bafa84 replicated 630.8/639.2): GET-inserted folios without history go to a separate JUNK list; first access list_move()s them to small tail. Eviction drains junk head first, then scan/small/main as before. Replaces the full-small-list junk walk; tests whether walk cost matters (main-list walk variant fba686fd dropped to 619).
REPLICATION of 372e2b1f (648.9), comment-only change: measuring noise; all my variants span 625-649

REPLICATE b87946a9 (probation-only junk filter, 656.05) unchanged + comment, to test whether +2.3% over same-host noop pair (640.96/641.42) is real before building on it. Reflection: scan-first eviction costs ~45 ops/s on pc252 (572e5ce9 = same filter + scan-first = 611)

knob on junk-list (6bd? parent=630.0): EPOCH_SHIFT 14->16, freq history halves every 65K GET accesses (~1x per run) instead of every 16K. Workload is static Zipfian (IRM) so near-pure LFU should be better.

structural 1/3 consumed-scan-first (base f3a2e20c S3-FIFO+tail): scan_pids pages -> scan FIFO; evict first those the scanner already read (consumed), keep unread readahead until 4096 scan-insertions old, GET-hit scan pages get CLOCK. Hypothesis (IOPS cap synthesis): scan-first lost because it evicted unconsumed readahead. pc318 noop=615.7

CROSS-HOST REPLICATION of captain-ahab b87946a9 (656 on pc252) unchanged on pc258. My best here: 372e2b1f 648.9 / 645.3 replicate. Tests whether junk-filter+kernel-fallback beats my freq-CLOCK on my host (ahab saw my design at 591/597 on pc252)

never-accessed-first for ALL folios (1-line change from b87946a9): scan-thread folios now also enter probation and are released to kernel on first access, so only never-read pages (GET readahead + scan readahead past scan end) are evicted early. Context: b87946a9 replicated 656.05/647.59 (mean 651.8) vs same-host noop 640.96/641.42 (mean 641.2) => +1.7%, small but both filter runs > both noop runs. knob on b87946a9 (GET-only junk filter, 656/648): PROBE_RESERVE 512->32. Hypothesis: gain scales with junk freed; 512 kept ~2MiB (~4% of cache) of never-read GET readahead; in-flight reads already skipped by uptodate check. Reflection on 7280f092 (all-folios probation = 647.66): refaults -10% but tput same; on pc252 tput tracks BYTES PER READ I/O (rios pinned ~11.5k): get_scan 12.5KB->500, freq-CLOCK 14.5KB->591, noop 15.9KB->641, filter 15.7KB->652 => IOPS-bound, never destroy scan readahead

knob on my junk-list+freq-history (936b9cff=630.4, EPOCH_SHIFT 16): small (probation, real once-read pages only) FIFO 10% -> 25% of cgroup pages. Kernel default gives inactive ~50%; with junk drained separately, a longer probation may catch more 2nd hits. Context: davy 372e2b1f cross-host on pc257 = 628.1, ties my family (630-639).

unexplored basin: reference mglru.c unchanged on pc318 (noop 615.7). Team evidence (ahab b87946a9, 2d090442) says scan pages are NOT junk and all scan-penalizing policies lose; MGLRU treats all accesses equally with generations+tiers+refault feedback

structural 1/3 on adaptive scan/GET partition: direction probe with FIXED scan floor 2048 pages (~17% of 47MiB cache) on 372e2b1f; scan FIFO only drained above floor (plus last-resort fallback). Motivation: scan-first +27 on pc258 but -45 on pc252 (ahab) => optimal scan residency is nonzero/host-dependent

knob shape: PROBE_RESERVE 2048 on b87946a9 base. Reflection on 36b60722 (reserve 32 = 627, -25 vs 512's mean 651.8, below noop 641): FALSIFIED 'unaccessed = junk' at short timescales; young unread GET readahead is often used later, so evicting it within ms wastes the I/O (fits IOPS-bound/bytes-per-IO story). Curve so far: 32->627, 512->652, inf(~noop)->641. This tests which side of 512 the peak is
sweep small FIFO size on junk-list+freq-history: 10%=630.4, 25%=639.1 -> now 50% (cache_size/2; main<=small guard also caps). Testing whether the trend continues toward kernel-like ~50% inactive.

structural 1/3 MGLRU lane: reference/mglru.c UNCHANGED (+comment) on pc252, cross-host replication of nemo's 657/669 on pc318 (+7.7% vs his noop 616). structural 1/3 MGLRU+refault activation: reference mglru.c (657.4/669.5 on pc318, noop 615.7) + kernel workingset rule: ghost stores eviction seq; page refaulting within 12288 evictions (~cgroup pages) re-enters youngest gen with 2 refs (protected). Ghost was stats-only before
CROSS-HOST: reference/mglru.c unchanged on pc258 (nemo: 657/669 on pc318 vs noop 616). pc258 noop=622.9, my best 372e2b1f=648.9/645.3

mglru 1/3 (parent = reference mglru.c, 685.06 on pc257): lru_gen_add_folio uses list_add_tail instead of list_add, so new folios sit at the END of their (oldest/2nd-oldest) generation instead of being the next eviction candidate. Rationale: mglru evicts never-read pages ~immediately (zero junk reserve); ahab's probation reserve curve 32->627, 512->656 says a grace period helps.

structural 2/3 on MGLRU: reference mglru.c + never-read reserve (newest 512 insertions with refs<=1 moved to next gen instead of evicted), grafting captain-ahab's reserve curve (32->627, 512->656) onto MGLRU's newest-unread-first eviction. pc318: MGLRU 657.4/669.5, noop 615.7

structural 2/3 MGLRU lane: fixed tier_threshold=0 (replaces PID-controller get_tier_idx) => any folio re-accessed after insertion is promoted to next gen on eviction pass (pure frequency protection for Zipf GET set; also protects scan-read pages). Base: unchanged mglru.c = 656.52 on pc252 (+2.4% vs same-host noop 641; bytes/IO 16.7KB highest seen). Reserve-graft lane left to captain-nemo to avoid overlap

mglru 2/3 (parent reference mglru.c = 685.06): new non-active folios always go to the OLDEST gen (seq=min_seq) instead of min_seq+1 when >2 gens; still list_add at head. Direction from mglru 1/3: tail-insert grace period = 601 (-12%), so being more aggressive on new folios may help.

structural 1/2: MGLRU (ref, 657.9 on pc258) + scan-first layer: scan_pids folios kept in a FIFO outside MGLRU and drained first on eviction; scan folio hit by a GET thread is list_del'd and lru_gen_add_folio'd into MGLRU. Loader now reuses harness scan_pids pin. Scan-first was +27 on pc258 in freq-CLOCK (d9050830 vs fe0ca4fc)

structural 3/3 on MGLRU: reference mglru.c + refs decay (protected folio refs-- on each promotion to next gen; refs never reset in reference so protection is permanent/LFU-like). Tests whether MGLRU's LFU-ness helps. pc318 MGLRU 657.4/669.5, noop 615.7

REPLICATION #2 of reference mglru.c on pc257 (first run 685.06; comment-only change). Needed because both my mglru perturbations lost (tail-insert 601.0, always-oldest-gen 653.8) - is 685 a high draw?

Reflection on 36f75f6a (threshold 0 = 639.03, -17.5 vs PID default 656.52): FALSIFIED static frequency protection; refaults fell 24.0k->18.3k and bytes/IO fell 16.7->14.5KB, the same signature as freq-CLOCK/get_scan on pc252 (more retention => smaller I/Os => lower tput). This tests the opposite direction

unexplored extreme: reference mru.c unchanged on pc318. Motivation: ahab 22bb52af MGLRU tier_threshold=3 (no freq protection, head-insert => evict newest-in-oldest-gen) 668.6 > default 656.5 > threshold0 639 on pc252: less retention => bigger IOs => more tput. MRU is the extreme of 'keep resident set, evict newcomers'. pc318: noop 615.7, MGLRU 657.4/669.5

FINAL eval, CROSS-HOST REPLICATION of captain-ahab 22bb52af (MGLRU, tier_threshold fixed at 3 = near-pure generational aging; 668.65 on pc252 vs unchanged MGLRU 656.5 there) on pc258. pc258 baselines: noop 622.85, MGLRU unchanged 657.94/654.84, my freq-CLOCK+probation 648.9/645.3
